title: Assistant Initiation Strategies — personal notebook
content:
Notes to self — rapid dump (chaotic, will refine)

Context / why this matters
- Many partners ask how the assistant should start interactions: short prompts, greeting + state, or full context dump. Starting behavior impacts perceived latency, cost, and initial relevance.
- We currently rely on client-driven start text (caller decides). There is opportunity to offer built-in initiation strategies in the API/SDK that trade off tokens vs. first-response quality.

High-level goal
- Provide a small set of configurable "initiation strategies" that developers can choose from or let Redwood autosuggest based on workload: minimal, contextual, hybrid, proactive.
- Make strategies easy to reason about (cost/latency tradeoffs), measurable, and safe (no PII leaks, obey privacy opt-outs).

Target users
- Product engineers building conversational features who want predictable startup UX without re-implementing heuristics.
- Platform teams standardizing assistant behavior across products.

Candidate strategies (naming working):
1) Minimal (hot-start): send a 1–2 sentence system instruction only. Fastest, lowest tokens. Good for ephemeral assistants or when client will immediately provide user input.
2) Full-context warmstart: send last N turns + user profile snippet + system instruction. Highest quality for follow-up tasks; higher token cost and latency.
3) Profile-leveraged: send system instruction plus compacted user profile/affinity vectors (embedding pointers) instead of raw chat. Medium cost, lower latency than full-context.
4) Proactive hinting: send minimal context + predicted user intent seed (from local model or heuristics) that primes the assistant to supply options/suggestions up-front. Useful for discovery flows.
5) On-demand enrich (lazy-load): start minimal and attach a small synchronously requested enrichment (e.g., recent transactions) if assistant signals need. Saves tokens but adds complexity.

User stories
- As a mobile app engineer, I want a low-cost default so new users see a reply quickly on slow networks. Acceptance: default initiation (minimal) yields median initial latency < 400ms on target fleet for small models.
- As an enterprise product manager, I want high-precision onboarding messaging using profile data. Acceptance: warmstart achieves 8%+ higher task success on onboarding flows vs minimal (A/B test).
- As a platform owner, I want a safe way to surface proactive suggestions without exposing PII. Acceptance: proactive hinting must pass redaction checks and have audit logs.

Metrics / what to measure
- Time-to-first-token (TTFT) / p50,p95
- Initial response quality (task success proxies, NPS, click-throughs)
- Token cost delta vs baseline per initiation strategy
- Percentage of requests that trigger on-demand enrichment
- Failure modes: refresh errors, privacy redaction hits

Acceptance criteria (MVP)
- API/SDK flag: initiation_strategy = [minimal|warmstart|profile|proactive|lazy]
- Server-side telemetry for each strategy (tokens, latency, success event mapping)
- Canary rollout path with per-tenant opt-in
- Basic safety checks: maximum context size, redaction pipeline for any profile fields included

Implementation sketch (back-of-envelope)
- API surface: include new optional fields in StartSession / ChatCreate: initiation_strategy, profile_id, enrichment_policy, hint_seed_override. SDK helpers to recommend strategy by device/network tier.
- Server: orchestration layer constructs prompt bundle from strategy template -> runtime applies prefix caching if warmstart repeated often -> consider KV cache keys per session template to reuse compiled prompts.
- Cache/batching implications: warmstart increases token reuse if many sessions share same profile. Consider enabling prefix sharing for private deployments with tenant isolation.

Experiment plan
- Phase A: internal dogfood on web + mobile with Metric: initial task completion rate. Compare minimal vs profile-leveraged for two onboarding flows. Duration 2 weeks.
- Phase B: small external customer pilot (3 customers) using warmstart for onboarding and proactive for help discovery. Monitor token costs, QA feedback.
- Phase C: wider rollout with SDK recommendations enabled.

Risks & open questions
- Privacy: what fields are ok to include in profile snippets? Need clear opt-in from customers.
- Cost blowout if customers default to warmstart. Mitigation: set quota warnings, expose monthly token impact estimate per app.
- Latency: warmstart could break tight p50 latency SLOs. Consider offering pre-warmed sessions for high-tier customers (dedicated).
- Edge cases: multi-device sync, session handoff. How to preserve semantics when session started on one device and resumed on another?

Operational notes
- Logging: tag every initiation with selected strategy, token delta, and redaction flags. Keep small sample of raw prompts for debugging behind secure audit logs.
- Rollout: start as opt-in, then make default minimal with suggested prompt templates in Console.

Next steps (todo)
- [ ] Draft API proposal and example payloads (RI-3121)
- [ ] Prototype SDK helper that picks strategy by connectivity + user stage (cold/new/returning)
- [ ] Build telemetry dashboards (Console) for strategy comparison
- [ ] Draft privacy checklist for profile snippet fields (legal review)

Random thoughts / rough heuristics
- On mobile, prefer "minimal + proactive hints" when RTT > 150ms.
- On trusted enterprise flows, allow warmstart by default but provide per-tenant cap on tokens used for initiations.
- We could experiment with an "initiation credit" bundle: first N session starts per user are free to encourage onboarding flows.

References / links I need to check later
- Existing prefix-cache design doc (GH link)
- Console feature: per-route token estimators (owner: Devon)
- Legal: data minimization guidance for Private deployments

End of dump. Will tidy into a short PRD and API spec next week.
